newsitem.title: MEXICO: Seven die in Mexico fireworks explosion.
newsitem.headline: Seven die in Mexico fireworks explosion.

text.p: Four children and three adults died in an explosion at a northern Mexico candy store that fronted as a clandestine fireworks warehouse, authorities said on Friday.

The four children were brothers and sisters between six months and seven years of age. They were visiting their aunt and uncle, the owners of the candy store in the border town of Reynosa, across the Rio Grande from McAllen, Texas.
Six others were injured in the blast late on Thursday. It ripped through the store and caused a fire as shoppers were making post-Christmas purchases.
Filadelfo Montesinos, spokesman for the Reynosa Civil Protection Force, said authorities were investigating whether fireworks were also manufactured at the store or only stored there.
"The explosion was caused by gunpowder that is used in the production of fireworks," Montesinos said.
The four brothers and sisters were Juan Manuel, Jose Guadalupe, and Alejandra and Isabel Guzman Acuna.
Three adults -- Martin Cardenas, Marcelo Castillo, and Maria Guadalupe John -- also died in the blast, which caused the roof of the store to collapse. Fire also damaged neighbouring houses.
Maria Isabel Acuna de Guzman, the mother of the four children, was one of those injured, authorities said.
